cases.label: G_ML_knowledge
cases.question: Why might a high learning rate create unstable training?
cases.answer:
### Relevant ML knowledge
- **Linear regression: Hyperparameters** (learning rates and optimization): The learning rate controls the size of a gradient-descent parameter update. A rate that is too high can make optimization bounce around a minimum or fail to converge; a rate that is too low can make progress slow. The useful rate depends on the model and data. This general mechanism does not establish why any specific Fashion-MNIST run changed.
- **Overfitting: Interpreting loss curves** (training and validation loss curves): Loss curves can oscillate or rise for several reasons. Reducing a learning rate can be useful when debugging an oscillating training-loss curve. When training loss improves but validation loss rises, overfitting is one possible interpretation. These are general diagnostic ideas, not proof of a cause for any particular saved run.

### Limitations
- A similarity or reranker score ranks text; it is not a probability or proof.

### Sources
**General ML references**
- [Linear regression: Hyperparameters](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/linear-regression/hyperparameters)
- [Overfitting: Interpreting loss curves](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/overfitting/interpreting-loss-curves)

- **baseline_gap_001** (note rank 1, cosine 0.4119): Validation loss rose from 0.8696 at epoch 1 to 1.4186 at epoch 2, then fell to 0.6663 at epoch 3. At epoch 5, post-epoch training loss was 0.8092 and validation loss was 0.8208.
  - Saved validation loss, epochs 1->2->3: 0.8696 -> 1.4186 -> 0.6663.

### Relevant ML knowledge
- **Optimizing Model Parameters** (SGD, loss, and weight updates): Optimization changes model parameters to reduce error. In PyTorch's training loop, zero_grad clears accumulated gradients, backward computes gradients of loss, and optimizer.step updates parameters. The SGD optimizer receives a learning-rate setting. A saved validation-loss curve records outcomes after those updates; it does not reveal every internal step.
- **Linear regression: Hyperparameters** (learning rates and optimization): The learning rate controls the size of a gradient-descent parameter update. A rate that is too high can make optimization bounce around a minimum or fail to converge; a rate that is too low can make progress slow. The useful rate depends on the model and data. This general mechanism does not establish why any specific Fashion-MNIST run changed.

### Possible interpretation
The observed pattern is compatible with one or more general mechanisms described above. The saved runs do not establish which mechanism, if any, caused it.
